title: Latency Tradecraft: 15s Opener Mini-Deck (Sketch)
body:
ASSUMPTION: seller/SE has 60–90s total. Goal: equip SE to open with a 15s latency tradecraft hook, then escalate to a 3-slide tech + one-liner demo.

Slide 1 — The 15s Opener (headline + framing)
- Headline (one liner): 'We help engineering teams get predictable LLM latency at scale — so product UX doesn't blame the model.'
- Why it matters in 15s: customer story hook: 'A fintech search team reduced tail latency spikes by 4x and reduced customer escalations by 37% after moving to a routing + cache plan.'
- Callout (speaker cue): drop an explicit latency number if customer gives an SLA (e.g., "If your median is 120ms, we can help push 50–70ms in typical configs").
- Note to SE: quick qualification prompt — "What's the tightest latency SLO you measure today?"

Speaker notes (condensed): keep it metric-forward, use one small human story, avoid product laundry lists. If buyer says "cost" or "accuracy" switch to a 2-line tradeoff frame: "We treat cost/accuracy/latency as a levered system — here are pragmatic levers (batching, KV cache, model variants)."

Slide 2 — Three micro-plays (15–30s each)
- Play A: "Latency-first routing"
  - Quick pitch: route 90% of requests to low-latency quantized model, 10% to higher-fidelity model for verification/fallback.
  - When to use: high-concurrency, user-facing features (chat, autofill).
  - SE prompt: ask about peak concurrency and acceptable quality variance.
- Play B: "Prefix caching for repeat contexts"
  - Quick pitch: caching KV for repeated prefixes reduces per-token time and cost for sessionized flows (support chat, agents).
  - When to use: conversation and form-fill where prompts repeat.
- Play C: "Dynamic batch sizing + SLO guardrails"
  - Quick pitch: autoscaling and micro-batching tuned to latency SLOs — we shift between batch modes to hit 95th/99th targets.
  - When to use: high-throughput inference (bulk embed jobs, analytics pipelines).

Slide 3 — Rapid demo/validation checklist (30–60s)
- If you have 2 min of time: show the latency dashboard for a sample route (highlight median, p95, p99).
- If not: run a quick ask: "Can you share 1) current median/p95 latency 2) tokens per request 3) peak RPS?"
- Quick validation heuristics (YES/NO):
  - If median > 200ms => strong latency pain (immediate hook)
  - If p99 > 1s => reliability risk, bring up fallbacks and routing
  - If peak RPS spikes > 2x baseline frequently => consider Dedicated/reserved approach

Appendix (for follow-up calls — talking bullets)
- Batching knobs: explain tradeoffs in plain language (larger batches = better cost but higher baseline latency; small/continuous batches reduce latency variability).
- Quantization profile: outline choice: 4-bit fast infer vs 8-bit fidelity tradeoffs; when to recommend each.
- Routing policies: region-aware, cost-aware, tier-aware (example YAML snippets exist in playbook link).

Objection scripts (quick, 1–2 lines)
- 'We care more about quality than latency' -> 'We route a small percentage to higher-fidelity models so your accuracy baseline is preserved while most traffic sees faster responses.'
- 'We already use batching' -> 'Great — we often find prefix caching and model variants reduce the need for large batches while improving tail behavior.'
- 'We can't share metrics' -> 'No problem — we can run a 48hr side-by-side with a small synthetic workload to show delta without access to prod.'

Internal playbook cues (notes to SE)
- When to call SRE/Platform partner in meeting: if customer mentions regulatory constraints (PII, on-prem), or p99 > 2s with sensitive workloads.
- Quick routing to product: if customer needs session-level encryption + HSM keys.
- Demo assets: link to short video of dashboard (30s), synthetic load script, p95/p99 comparison chart template.

Open questions for GTM alignment (for this deck iteration)
- Does AE/SDR training want a 60s variant for SDR outreach? (I think yes — we should create a one-liner pack.)
- Can we standardize two story templates: e-comm checkout and fintech search for faster reuse?
- Need product-approved numbers for 'typical improvement ranges' to avoid overpromising.

To-do (next edits)
- Add 30s dashboard GIF (Ravi)
- Create a one-liner SLA table (Sofia)
- Add quick YAML snippet for routing policy example (Jordan)

Quick raw notes / scratch (choppy):
- 15s opener must be metric + human ("we cut tail latency -> fewer user drop-offs")
- keep demo < 2 min or bring to follow-up
- include fallback/rollback language for enterprise buyers
- runtime knobs = best seller lever (cost vs latency tradeoff)

Related artifacts and references (links in linked_artifacts): see Confluence playbook, Jira for sample test harness, GH PR with dashboard export.

END OF SKETCH — this is intentionally light and rough, meant to be converted into 3 clean slides + one pager for SDRs.
